I manage IT for a small business in Indiana. We rent out the Cafe space at the local library as one of our retail outlets. We have a lease with said library, and contained in that lease is a clause that the library will manage physical security for the space we rent. Despite this, we have seen a rash of thefts after hours in the past few days. Because the library is closed when this happens, its either a librarian, janitor, security guard, or caterer (the lobby, where the cafe is located, is rented out for weddings and events and whatnot in the evenings, after we are gone. The caterers officially are not allowed to use or be in our space, but according to the cleaning staff, they regularly are, and equipment is regularly unplugged, dirty, or damaged, when it was plugged in, clean and functional when our employees left the previous day) doing this. When we have approached security (which is contracted out through a local company), the footage, which we were not permitted to see firsthand, was "Too blurry" to determine a culprit (Surprisingly, it was clear enough for them to identify one of our employees working without gloves several months back, even though our gloves are almost entirely transparent. Not that i'm mad that they caught that, its a good thing, just an interesting observation about allegedly inconsistent quality of footage). As such, the business owner has asked me, as the one man IT department, to set up security cameras in the cafe. And she wants me to do it WITHOUT informing the library, as she doesn't want to confront the library administrators, who have been very generous and easy to work with, with allegations about their contractors and employees, nor about the effectiveness of security, which has been on contract far longer than we have been.

Aside from the logistics of having to record footage to a device without putting it on the network (plus, I really do NOT want to put my equipment in a food service area, where debris, liquids, and other random shit gets everywhere, regardless of the risk of putting something with lots of blinky lights in an area that's already been broken into, and is not restricted access in any way- in addition to a disturbing number of keys, people can just jump over the counter, there's no security grille.), this seems rather... concerning from a legal perspective; that is to say, putting recording devices in a leased portion of a public space, the field of view of which will doubtless extend beyond the rented space, all without telling the landlord. Can anyone give me information on the legality of such things? Bearing in mind that this is a commercial lease, not a residential one....

(and before I get waves upon waves of hate, I'm all for telling the library; They were so generous with the lease, we shouldn't be acting behind their back. Sadly, this is not my call, though i'm trying to convince the business owner to see it from my perspective.)
